facts.fact: Nairametrics reports Nigeria's National Broadband Plan 2020-2025 expired in December 2025, four months before the article, though an NCC commissioner said the plan 'has not ended'.
NCC Executive Commissioner Abraham Oshadami said the regulator is reviewing the old plan's performance and is coming up with a new plan to succeed it.
The article sets NCC data of 51.97% broadband penetration (December 2025) against the plan's 70% target, and 52.95% of mobile subscriptions on 4G against its 70%-by-2023 milestone.
ATCON's president cites the Federal Government's ongoing push to support deployment of about 7,000 telecom towers in underserved and unserved areas, with no sites yet counted as connected.

NGA.note: Project BRIDGE is named as delivering part of the old strategy, with no contract, works or service stated.
The article says Nigeria has no local smartphone assembly plant; the study has no value for that and no ICT export figure is given.
Only broadband penetration and 4G subscription shares are given, not the share of people using the internet.
